DE.name: Germany
DE.baselineNote: UBA average, consumption-based (imports included). Point estimate, UBA publishes no range.

options.label: Car for everything
options.basis: About 50% more car-km than average (~+3,500 km/yr at ~0.2 kg CO2e/km incl. fuel supply).

options.label: Average
options.basis: Average mix of car, public transport, bike and walking.

options.label: Mostly public transport
options.basis: About 60% of car-km shifted to bus and rail, which emit 3 to 4 times less per passenger-km.

options.label: Bike & walk
options.basis: Almost no car-km. UBA: replacing two 5 km car trips a day with cycling alone saves up to 0.5 t.

dimensions.label: Car type
dimensions.note: The effect scales with how much you drive.

options.label: Large petrol/diesel or SUV
options.basis: ~0.28 kg CO2e/km vs ~0.17 for an average car (DESNZ), at average car-km.

options.label: Average car
options.basis: Average German car fleet.

options.label: Small car
options.basis: ~0.14 kg CO2e/km for a small petrol car, plus lower manufacturing emissions.

options.label: Electric car
options.basis: ~18 kWh/100 km on the German grid mix (~0.36 kg/kWh) plus battery manufacturing: roughly half of an average car.

options.label: No flights
options.basis: Removes the average per-person flight share (~0.5 t incl. non-CO2 effects).

options.label: 1 short-haul return
options.basis: e.g. Berlin to Barcelona and back: ~3,000 km at ~0.13 kg CO2e/pkm incl. non-CO2 effects, ~0.4 t.

options.label: Average
options.basis: Average across all people, including the many who never fly.

options.label: 1 long-haul return
options.basis: e.g. Frankfurt to New York and back: ~12,400 km at ~0.15 kg CO2e/pkm (economy, incl. non-CO2), ~1.9 to 2.5 t. Stronger non-CO2 weighting gives up to ~4 t.

options.label: Frequent flyer (3+ long-haul)
options.basis: Three or more long-haul returns a year, or many short trips.

categories.label: Housing
categories.note: Heating and hot water. Heat pump electricity is counted here.

options.label: Oil
options.basis: Heating oil ~0.32 vs natural gas ~0.25 kg CO2e/kWh incl. supply chain (~30% more).

options.label: Gas
options.basis: Natural gas is the most common heating type in Germany.

options.label: District heat
options.basis: Depends heavily on the local plant: from coal-fired (no saving) to waste heat or biomass.

options.label: Heat pump
options.basis: Seasonal efficiency ~3 on the German grid (~0.36 kg/kWh) gives ~0.12 kg per kWh of heat, about half of gas.

options.label: Unrenovated
options.basis: Older buildings without retrofit use roughly 30 to 50% more heat than the average stock.

options.label: Average
options.basis: Average German building stock.

options.label: Well insulated
options.basis: Good insulation saves 0.5 t+ per person per year (UBA).

options.label: Large (70 m²+ per person)
options.basis: Heat demand grows roughly with floor area; ~50% more space than the average of ~47 m² per person.

options.label: Average (~47 m²)
options.basis: Average living space per person in Germany.

options.label: Small or shared (<30 m²)
options.basis: Less floor area per person to heat; shared flats split the heating of common space.

options.label: Warm (22 °C+)
options.basis: Rule of thumb: each 1 °C warmer adds about 6% heating energy.

options.label: Average (20 °C)
options.basis: Typical living-room temperature.

options.label: Cooler (19 °C)
options.basis: Each 1 °C less saves about 6% heating energy: a classic quick win.

categories.label: Electricity
categories.note: Household electricity only. Electric cars and heat pumps are counted in Mobility and Housing.

options.label: High (many devices, dryer)
options.basis: About 50% above the average of ~1,500 kWh per person.

options.label: Average (~1,500 kWh)
options.basis: ~1,500 kWh per person at the German grid mix (~0.36 kg/kWh).

options.label: Low (efficient, mindful)
options.basis: About 35% below average with efficient appliances and no standby.

options.label: Grid mix
options.basis: German grid mix.

options.label: Green tariff
options.basis: Wide range: the saving depends on whether the tariff funds new renewables or only buys certificates.

options.label: Own solar
options.basis: Rooftop PV covering ~50 to 60% of own use at ~0.04 kg CO2e/kWh (lifecycle).

options.label: Meat-heavy
options.basis: Meat most days, often beef. Beef is ~100 kg CO2e/kg vs ~10 for chicken (Poore & Nemecek).

options.label: Mixed
options.basis: Average German diet.

options.label: Flexitarian
options.basis: Meat about once or twice a week.

options.label: Vegetarian
options.basis: UBA: switching from a mixed to a vegetarian diet saves about 0.4 t a year.

options.label: Vegan
options.basis: UBA: a vegan diet saves about 0.8 t a year compared to a mixed diet.

options.label: High
options.basis: Throwing away about twice the average (~75 kg of household food waste per person a year).

options.label: Average
options.basis: Average household food waste.

options.label: Low
options.basis: Planning, using leftovers, buying less: most avoidable waste avoided.

categories.label: Consumption
categories.note: Clothing, electronics, furniture, household goods and leisure.

options.label: Fashion lover
options.basis: Buying 2 to 3 times the average amount of new clothes (EU average ~0.27 t a year).

options.label: Average
options.basis: EU textile consumption ~270 kg CO2e per person a year (EEA).

options.label: Conscious (wear longer)
options.basis: Wearing clothes 1 to 2 years longer cuts their footprint by about 24% (Carbon Trust).

options.label: Mostly second hand
options.basis: Most new purchases replaced by second-hand ones: up to about two thirds of the average.

options.label: New every year
options.basis: A new smartphone (~60 to 80 kg) and a laptop or tablet (~200 to 300 kg) every year.

options.label: Average
options.basis: Typical replacement cycles.

options.label: Use long, buy refurbished
options.basis: Most of a device's footprint is manufacturing; doubling its life roughly halves it.

options.label: Buy a lot new
options.basis: Frequent new furniture, gadgets, hobby gear, hotels and events.

options.label: Average
options.basis: Average German consumption.

options.label: Buy less, repair, borrow
options.basis: UBA: about 2 t can be saved across all consumption by repairing, borrowing, buying less and used. This is the share outside clothing and electronics.

categories.label: Public infrastructure
categories.note: Roads, schools, hospitals, administration. No individual choice changes this share; it is the case for policy.

equivalents.label: beef steaks (200 g)
equivalents.basis: Beef from beef herds, ~100 kg CO2e/kg.

equivalents.label: tree seedlings grown for 10 years
equivalents.basis: EPA: one urban tree seedling grown for 10 years absorbs ~0.06 t CO2.

US.name: USA
US.baselineNote: Sources range from about 14 to 17+ t; the category split is a project estimate cross-checked against CoolClimate and UMich CSS. Needs one primary source before launch.

options.label: Car for everything
options.basis: About 30% more vehicle-miles than the already high US average.

options.label: Average
options.basis: Average US travel mix, mostly by car.

options.label: Mostly public transport
options.basis: About 60% of car-miles shifted to bus and rail.

options.label: Bike & walk
options.basis: Almost no car-miles.

dimensions.label: Car type
dimensions.note: The effect scales with how much you drive.

options.label: Pickup or large SUV
options.basis: Roughly 30% more fuel per mile than the average US light-duty vehicle.

options.label: Average car
options.basis: Typical passenger vehicle, ~0.4 kg CO2/mile (EPA).

options.label: Small or hybrid
options.basis: About 25% less fuel per mile.

options.label: Electric car
options.basis: ~0.3 kWh/mile on the US grid (~0.37 kg/kWh, eGRID) plus battery manufacturing.

options.label: No flights
options.basis: Removes the average per-person flight share (~1 t incl. non-CO2 effects).

options.label: 1 domestic return
options.basis: e.g. New York to Chicago and back: ~2,300 km, ~0.4 to 0.6 t incl. non-CO2 effects.

options.label: Average
options.basis: Average across all people, including those who never fly.

options.label: 1 long-haul return
options.basis: e.g. New York to London and back: ~11,100 km, ~1.7 t incl. non-CO2, on top of some domestic flying.

options.label: Frequent flyer (3+ long-haul)
options.basis: Three or more long-haul returns a year, or many domestic trips.

categories.label: Housing
categories.note: Heating and hot water. Heat pump and electric heating electricity is counted here.

options.label: Oil
options.basis: Heating oil emits ~30% more per kWh of heat than natural gas.

options.label: Gas
options.basis: Natural gas is the most common US heating fuel.

options.label: Electric resistance
options.basis: Baseboard or furnace heating on the US grid (~0.37 kg/kWh) emits more than gas.

options.label: Heat pump
options.basis: Seasonal efficiency ~3 on the US grid: roughly half the emissions of gas.

options.label: Older, drafty
options.basis: About 30% more heat demand than the average home.

options.label: Average
options.basis: Average US housing stock.

options.label: Well insulated
options.basis: About 30% less heat demand after insulation and air sealing.

options.label: Large house
options.basis: About 40% more floor area per person than average.

options.label: Average
options.basis: Average US living space per person.

options.label: Small or shared
options.basis: Apartment or shared home with about 30% less space per person.

options.label: Warm (72 °F+)
options.basis: Each 1 °C (~2 °F) warmer adds about 6% heating energy.

options.label: Average (68 °F)
options.basis: Typical thermostat setting.

options.label: Cooler (66 °F)
options.basis: Each 1 °C (~2 °F) less saves about 6% heating energy.

categories.label: Electricity
categories.note: Household electricity incl. air conditioning. Electric cars and electric heating are counted in Mobility and Housing.

options.label: High (lots of AC, large home)
options.basis: About 50% above the average of ~4,500 kWh per person.

options.label: Average (~4,500 kWh)
options.basis: ~4,500 kWh per person at ~0.39 kg/kWh (eGRID incl. losses).

options.label: Low (efficient, mindful)
options.basis: About a third below average with efficient appliances and moderate AC.

options.label: Grid mix
options.basis: US average grid (eGRID).

options.label: Green tariff
options.basis: Wide range: the saving depends on whether the program adds new renewables or only buys certificates (RECs).

options.label: Own solar
options.basis: Rooftop PV covering ~60% of own use at ~0.04 kg CO2e/kWh (lifecycle).

options.label: Meat-heavy
options.basis: Meat most days, often beef (~100 kg CO2e/kg, Poore & Nemecek).

options.label: Mixed
options.basis: Average US diet.

options.label: Flexitarian
options.basis: Meat about once or twice a week.

options.label: Vegetarian
options.basis: US meat consumption is higher than German, so the saving is larger.

options.label: Vegan
options.basis: No animal products.

options.label: High
options.basis: Wasting well above the US average, where about 30% of food is wasted.

options.label: Average
options.basis: Average household food waste.

options.label: Low
options.basis: Planning, using leftovers, buying less.

categories.label: Consumption
categories.note: Goods and services: clothing, electronics, furniture, household goods and leisure.

options.label: Fashion lover
options.basis: Buying 2 to 3 times the average amount of new clothes.

options.label: Average
options.basis: US clothing consumption, assumed ~0.35 t a year (above the EU 0.27 t).

options.label: Conscious (wear longer)
options.basis: Wearing clothes 1 to 2 years longer cuts their footprint by about 24% (Carbon Trust).

options.label: Mostly second hand
options.basis: Most new purchases replaced by second-hand ones.

options.label: New every year
options.basis: A new phone, laptop or tablet and other gadgets every year.

options.label: Average
options.basis: Typical replacement cycles.

options.label: Use long, buy refurbished
options.basis: Most of a device's footprint is manufacturing; doubling its life roughly halves it.

options.label: Buy a lot new
options.basis: Frequent new furniture, gadgets, hobby gear, hotels and events.

options.label: Average
options.basis: Average US goods and services.

options.label: Buy less, repair, borrow
options.basis: Repairing, borrowing, buying less and used, scaled from the UBA estimate for Germany.

categories.label: Public infrastructure
categories.note: Roads, schools, hospitals, defense, administration. No individual choice changes this share; it is the case for policy.

equivalents.label: beef steaks (7 oz)
equivalents.basis: Beef from beef herds, ~100 kg CO2e/kg.

equivalents.label: tree seedlings grown for 10 years
equivalents.basis: EPA: one urban tree seedling grown for 10 years absorbs ~0.06 t CO2.
